name: Read it out
desc: Speech, a file written and a folder opened -- all of it .NET, and not one line of code in the whole program. The text box is bound to a value, every button is a rule, and the four things it does are .NET methods made into your own functions on App > Libraries. The one that talks runs in the background, so the window keeps answering while it does.
vars:
words = "Hello from AutoHotkey, by way of the .NET Framework."
filename = A_Desktop "\spoken.txt"
howMany <- StrLen(words) " character" (StrLen(words) = 1 ? "" : "s")
hasWords <- (Trim(words) != "")

windows.name: Main
windows.title: Read it out
windows.status:
msg | Type something and press Read it out | grow icon=E767
count |  | right dim
windows.flows:
readBtn Click -> call Speak words
readBtn Click -> status msg Read it out loud.
saveBtn Click -> call SaveText filename, words
saveBtn Click -> status msg Saved.
saveBtn Click -> toast Saved
loadBtn Click -> assign words ReadBack filename
loadBtn Click -> status msg Read back from the file.
openBtn Click -> call OpenIt filename
clearBtn Click -> assign words 
clearBtn Click -> status msg Cleared.
windows.binds:
textBox <-> words
whereBox <-> filename
countLabel.Text <- howMany
readBtn.Enabled <- hasWords
saveBtn.Enabled <- hasWords
clearBtn.Enabled <- hasWords

kids.name: tip
kids.arg: Nothing in this program is written by hand. The text box is kept in step with a value, the buttons are rules -- when this is clicked, do that -- and the four things it does are .NET methods made into your own functions on App > Libraries. Reading aloud runs in the background, so the window answers while it talks.

props.title: No code, and all of it is .NET.

kids.name: textBox
kids.arg: Type anything here and press Read it out. Windows says it in its own voice, through System.Speech -- and because that one is set to run in the background, this window keeps answering while it talks.

props.placeholder: Where to save it -- a full path

adaptors:
Speak | new |  | System.Speech.Synthesis.SpeechSynthesizer.Speak | textToSpeak:string | void@async | Say it out loud, in Windows' own voice
SaveText | static |  | System.IO.File.WriteAllText | path:string, contents:string | void | Write text to a file, making it if it is not there
ReadBack | static |  | System.IO.File.ReadAllText | path:string | object | Read a whole file back as text
OpenIt | static |  | System.Diagnostics.Process.Start | fileName:string | object | Open something the way Windows would -- a file, a folder, a web page
